<TITLE>EX-99.1</TITLE>

 <BODY BGCOLOR="WHITE" STYLE="line-height:Normal">

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="right"><B>Exhibit 99.1 </B></P> <P STYLE="font-size:24pt;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt">&nbsp;</P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt" ALIGN="center">


<IMG SRC="g70523dsp0001.jpg" ALT="LOGO">
 </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>Atrium Therapeutics to Present Nonclinical Data Showing ATR 1072 </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>Reversed and Improved Features of PRKAG2 Syndrome During HCMS </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><B>at AHA Scientific Sessions 2026 </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>&#8212; ATR 1072 impacted key characteristics of PRKAG2 syndrome, including accumulation of </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>cardiac glycogen and cardiac hypertrophy &#8212; </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>&#8212; Data further reinforce scientific rationale for ATR 1072 targeting the root cause of </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>PRKAG2 syndrome &#8212; </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman" ALIGN="center"><I>&#8212; Poster presentation November&nbsp;6 at 5:30 p.m. CT &#8212; </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">SAN DIEGO, Nov. 2, 2026 &#8211; Atrium Therapeutics, Inc. (Nasdaq: RNA) (the &#8220;Company&#8221;), a&nbsp;biopharmaceutical company&nbsp;advancing precision
cardiology by developing&nbsp;RNA therapeutics targeted&nbsp;to the heart, today announced that it will present new nonclinical data supporting its lead investigational therapy ATR 1072 for the potential treatment of PRKAG2 (Protein Kinase <FONT
STYLE="white-space:nowrap">AMP-activated</FONT> <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-catalytic</FONT> subunit Gamma 2) syndrome during Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy Medical Society at the American Heart Association Scientific Sessions 2026, taking
place on November&nbsp;6, 2026, in Chicago, Illinois. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">&#8220;Our new nonclinical model reproduced many features of PRKAG2 syndrome, including cardiac
glycogen accumulation in the heart,&#8221; said Husam Younis, Chief Scientific Officer of Atrium Therapeutics. &#8220;We are encouraged to see that a mouse-specific version of ATR 1072 reversed cardiac glycogen accumulation and improved other key
features of the disease. These findings continue to strengthen the scientific rationale for ATR 1072. We now look to the ongoing Phase 1/2 Corventis trial and expect initial proof of concept data in the second half of 2027.&#8221; </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">The nonclinical results being presented at HCMS were generated in a new mouse model of PRKAG2 syndrome developed by Atrium that demonstrates key features of
the disease, including cardiac glycogen accumulation, cardiac hypertrophy, and electrocardiogram (ECG) abnormalities. In the study, mice received a single dose of mATR 1072, a mouse surrogate of ATR 1072, after features of the disease had been
established for three weeks. By targeting disease causing variant PRKAG2 mRNA in the heart, mATR 1072 treatment led to reversal of cardiac glycogen accumulation as well as improvement in other key features of the disease, including hypertrophy and
ECG parameters. </P>
</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt" ALIGN="center">


<IMG SRC="g70523dsp0001.jpg" ALT="LOGO">
 </P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Details of the HCMS Scientific Sessions poster: </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><U>Friday, November&nbsp;6, 2026, at 5:30 p.m CT. </U></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Targeting PRKAG2 mRNA with mATR 1072 to improve glycogen-storage cardiomyopathy in a mouse model of PRKAG2 syndrome</B><I> </I><B> </B></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><I>Presentation Number: HCM32; Poster Board Number: 32 </I></P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About PRKAG2 Syndrome </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">PRKAG2 syndrome is a rare,
autosomal dominant, early-onset cardiomyopathy caused by variants in the PRKAG2 gene, which encodes the Gamma 2 regulatory subunit of AMPK. Variants enhance AMPK activity leading to abnormal glycogen accumulation in the heart, thickened heart
muscles, electrical conduction problems, and arrhythmias. Based on current scientific literature estimates, there are at least 1,000 &#8211; 2,000 people with PRKAG2 syndrome in the US. Current management is limited to symptomatic treatment; no
approved therapies exist to address the underlying genetic driver of disease. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About the
Corventis<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> Trial </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Corventis<SUP STYLE="font-size:75%; vertical-align:top">&#153;</SUP> is a
Phase 1/2 open-label, multicenter clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy of ATR 1072 in participants living with PRKAG2 syndrome. The study will enroll approximately 37
participants across two parts: Part A, multiple ascending dose cohorts to characterize safety and support dose selection, and Part B, a <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">single-arm</FONT> expansion cohort at the recommended Phase 2 dose to further
evaluate efficacy trends in cardiac structure and function. The study&#8217;s primary endpoint is the incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events, with secondary and exploratory endpoints such as PRKAG2 mRNA reduction, siRNA tissue concentrations
and plasma pharmacokinetics. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Additional information about the trial is available at www.corventistrial.com. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>About Atrium Therapeutics </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">Atrium Therapeutics, Inc.
(Nasdaq: RNA) is pioneering targeted delivery of ribonucleic acid (RNA) therapeutics to the heart to transform the standard of care for people living with cardiomyopathies. The Company&#8217;s proprietary technology&#8212;designed at Avidity
Biosciences, Inc. - combines the tissue selectivity of monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and other targeted delivery ligands with the precision of oligonucleotides and is designed to </P>
</DIV></Center>


<p style="margin-top:1em; margin-bottom:0em; page-break-before:always"> </p>
<HR SIZE="3" style="COLOR:#999999" WIDTH="100%" ALIGN="CENTER">

<Center><DIV STYLE="width:8.5in" align="left">

 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt" ALIGN="center">


<IMG SRC="g70523dsp0001.jpg" ALT="LOGO">
 </P> <p STYLE="margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:0pt ; font-size:8pt">&nbsp;</P>
 <P STYLE="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">
selectively target the underlying drivers of genetically driven cardiac diseases through targeted, <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-viral</FONT> delivery of small interfering RNA (siRNA).
This approach builds upon learnings from demonstrated delivery to skeletal muscle and applies it for efficient delivery to the heart, with the potential to overcome challenges associated with <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-specific</FONT>
tissue delivery. The Company&#8217;s pipeline includes ATR 1072 for PRKAG2 syndrome, ATR 1086 for PLN (phospholamban) cardiomyopathy and two undisclosed research targets in rare cardiomyopathies. </P>
<P STYLE="margin-top:12pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">For more information about our RNA delivery platform, development pipeline and people, please visit&nbsp;https://atriumtherapeutics.com/ and engage with us
on&nbsp;LinkedIn. </P> <P STYLE="margin-top:18pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman"><B>Forward-Looking Statements </B></P> <P STYLE="margin-top:6pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt; font-family:Times New Roman">This
press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the United States Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Forward-looking statements can generally be identified by words such as &#8220;potential,&#8221;
&#8220;can,&#8221; &#8220;will,&#8221; &#8220;plan,&#8221; &#8220;may,&#8221; &#8220;could,&#8221; &#8220;would,&#8221; &#8220;expect,&#8221; &#8220;anticipate,&#8221; &#8220;look forward,&#8221; &#8220;believe,&#8221; &#8220;committed,&#8221;

contains forward-looking information relating to our planned presentation of nonclinical data at the HCMS Scientific Sessions 2026; the extent to which our new nonclinical model is representative of human PRKAG2 syndrome, and the extent to which
nonclinical results observed with mATR1072, a mouse surrogate of ATR 1072, support the scientific rationale for ATR 1072 or may be predictive of results in humans; the design, conduct, enrollment and anticipated progress of the Corventis Phase 1/2
clinical trial, including the expected number of participants; the therapeutic potential of ATR 1072, including its potential to address the underlying genetic cause of PRKAG2 syndrome; the potential of our targeted RNA delivery platform, including
its potential to deliver siRNA to the heart and to overcome challenges associated with <FONT STYLE="white-space:nowrap">non-specific</FONT> tissue delivery; our estimates of the prevalence of PRKAG2 syndrome; the potential implications of Corventis
